ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of each UBO, director, officer, and principal shareholder against: (1) the FIC Act targeted financial sanctions lists implementing UN Security Council resolutions; (2) the domestic South African designations under the Protection of Constitutional Democracy Against Terrorist and Related Activities Act, 2004; (3) the United Nations Consolidated List; (4) OFAC SDN, UK, and EU restrictive measures for cross-border correspondent banking; and (5) the Financial Intelligence Centre's domestic PEP indicators and prescribed lists. PEP status (foreign, domestic, and state-owned enterprise officials) requires enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring under FIC Act sections 21D-21H and FIC Directive 3. South Africa's FATF grey-listing (February 2023) imposes intensified CDD for high-risk sectors, including verification of UBO ownership and control, event-driven sanctions re-screening, and maintenance of a documented risk-based AML/CFT programme aligned with FIC Guidance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) online transactional portal (CIPC e-Services / BizPortal, accessible via www.cipc.co.za or www.gov.za)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name may be expressed in any of the twelve official South African languages but must be transliterated into Latin/Roman alphabetic script for electronic registration. The name must be unique, not confusingly similar to any existing company name, registered trademark, or reserved name, and must not be offensive or falsely suggest government, regulatory, or financial-sector endorsement. A private company must terminate its legal name with '(Pty) Ltd'. Non-Latin-script names appearing in UBO supporting documents require an apostilled certified translation into English for CIPC and FSCA records.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 20 business days of a CIPC name-rejection notice, the applicant may file a prescribed objection or reconsideration request via the CIPC e-Services dispute module, attaching a motivation and any supporting trademark or regulatory consents. If the rejection is upheld, the applicant may apply to the Companies Tribunal under section 160 of the Companies Act, 2008 and Companies Regulation 25 within 20 business days of the CIPC final decision, requesting a name review and hearing. The Tribunal may set aside or confirm the CIPC decision. Further review lies to the High Court of South Africa on administrative-law grounds under the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act, 2000, within 180 days of the Tribunal decision. Concurrently, the applicant may submit a fresh name application with a new CIPC reservation fee while the appeal is pending.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: CIPC accepts a domestic physical service-address virtual office as the registered office under section 23(3) of the Companies Act, provided it is a real geographic address in South Africa where statutory records are kept and legal process can be served. However, for a licensed equity-crowdfunding portal, the FSCA 'fit and proper' licensing framework and FIC Act accountable-institution duties require genuine local operational substance, including management presence, board records, compliance infrastructure, and a physical audit trail. A mailbox-only or forwarding-only virtual office is not permissible and would be treated as non-compliance, creating CIPC deregistration and FSCA licence-rejection risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 75 percent probability during the first 18 months of operation, driven by FSCA supervisory on-site inspections, FIC AML/CFT monitoring visits, and SARS compliance audits; FATF grey-list action plans further elevate the risk of unannounced inspections for high-risk financial-services entities such as crowdfunding intermediaries.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended by the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024, sections 13 (incorporation), 19 (legal personality), 23(3) (registered office), 35 (crowdfunding), 66 (board of directors) and 70 (first directors); read with the Financial Advisory and Intermediary Services Act 37 of 2002 (FAIS) for the platform licence.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), an agency of the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (DTIC), Pretoria, South Africa.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1A) and consent forms CoR 14.2 / CoR 14.3.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the Companies Act 71 of 2008; one or more shares (commonly ZAR 1.00 par value) may be issued. However, the FSCA crowdfunding framework requires minimum financial soundness, generally ZAR 5 million in unencumbered capital or an equivalent bank guarantee, with investor subscription funds held in a separate FICA-compliant escrow client account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscribers adopt the Memorandum of Incorporation and subscribe for 100 ordinary shares at ZAR 1.00 each, payment to be made into the company's bank account. FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office be established at 1 Finance Boulevard, Sandton, Johannesburg, South Africa, with postal address at the same location. FURTHER RESOLVED that Thabo Dlamini be appointed as sole Director and Chief Executive Officer, Lerato Nkosi as Chief Financial Officer, and Pieter van der Merwe as Company Secretary, each holding office until the next annual general meeting. FURTHER RESOLVED that the Directors are authorised to file the Notice of Incorporation with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission, to open corporate and client escrow bank accounts, and to prepare and lodge the Financial Sector Conduct Authority crowdfunding licence application. FURTHER RESOLVED that the Company Secretary issue share certificates and maintain all statutory registers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Login to CIPC e-Services and complete Form CoR 9.1 for name reservation, submitting two preferred names in ranked order and paying the statutory fee of ZAR 50 (plus VAT). The proposed name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name or trademark. Upon approval, the name remains reserved for six months, during which the incorporation must be lodged.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of incorporator's ID or passport
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for confusing similarity, file a fresh CoR 9.1 with alternate names or lodge a name dispute under section 160 of the Companies Act; the reservation may be renewed once before expiry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Memorandum of Incorporation and Consent Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel, proposed directors and proposed company secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Incorporation (CoR 14.1A) containing prescribed provisions, including share classes, voting rights, restrictions, and the special resolution thresholds. Prepare Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation), Form CoR 14.2 (Consent to Act as Director) for each director, and Form CoR 14.3 (Consent of Company Secretary or Auditor). All signatories must execute the documents by hand or with an advanced electronic signature compliant with the Electronic Communications and Transactions Act.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 14.2 from each proposed director
Form CoR 14.3 from company secretary or auditor
Certified ID copies of all directors and incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any drafting defect identified by CIPC is corrected by filing an amended MOI via Form CoR 15.1 within 20 business days after the notice of rejection; otherwise the incorporation application lapses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Lodgment with CIPC and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC Registration Division (e-Services or walk-in centre, Pretoria)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the CoR 14.1, CoR 14.1A and consent forms into CIPC e-Services, pay the incorporation fee of ZAR 175 (approximately USD 10), authorise the transaction and submit. CIPC verifies the filing against the Companies Act and issues the electronic Certificate of Incorporation, upon which the company acquires juristic personality and limited liability from the filing date.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC queries the submission, the applicant must correct the defective document and resubmit through e-Services within 20 business days; failure to do so lapses the application, requiring re-filing with new fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SARS Tax, UIF and FIC Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS eFiling), Department of Employment and Labour (UIF), and Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company with SARS for income tax, VAT (compulsory where annual taxable turnover exceeds ZAR 1 million), PAYE and UIF for future employees, and obtain a tax compliance status. Concurrently file the FIC accountable institution registration as an equity crowdfunding platform to satisfy the AML/CFT prerequisite for the FSCA licence. Confirm the company's public interest score, as an annual audit will be mandatory under FAIS/FSCA rules.
required_dossiers: Directors' certified ID or passport copies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS or FIC rejects or defers registration, verify the taxpayer or reporting profile, resubmit corrected supporting documents, and escalate through the SARS branch consultation service or the FIC contact centre.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: FSCA Equity Crowdfunding Platform Licence Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA), Licensing Division, Pretoria
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the FAIS Act Financial Services Provider (FSP) licence application under the Crowdfunding Platform category, including the business plan, section 17 compliance manual, AML/CFT framework, financial soundness evidence (ZAR 5 million unencumbered capital or guarantee), and fit-and-proper declarations for directors and key individuals. The FSCA assesses the application within up to 120 days and issues a restricted FSP licence with conditions; investor funds must be held in an escrow account from the date of licensing.
required_dossiers: Detailed business plan and revenue model
AML/CFT policy and FIC registration confirmation
Financial soundness proof (capital or bank guarantee)
Company MOI and Certificate of Incorporation
PAIA manual and internal complaints resolution framework
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FSCA issues a query, respond with full documentation within 30 days; if the licence is refused, lodge a reconsideration or appeal under section 9 FAIS, or reapply once identified deficiencies are cured.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA) — Licensing Division; co-regulator: Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC) for AML/CFT supervision
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Financial Services Provider (FSP) Licence — Crowdfunding Platform, a restricted FSP licence under the FAIS Act 37 of 2002 read with section 35 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 (as amended), endorsed for equity crowdfunding portal operations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) and City of Johannesburg Environmental Planning Department
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 — EIA Registration / Exemption for low-impact office-based fintech use under Listing Notice 3 of the EIA Regulations 2014 (as amended); no full environmental impact assessment or environmental authorisation required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial effluent or VOC emissions; domestic sewage only to municipal sewer per Water Services Act bylaws and SANS 10252-1; standby generator emissions compliant with the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act 39 of 2004 thresholds; general waste and e-waste handled under the National Waste Information Regulations 2012, with e-waste recycled by registered recyclers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate per SANS 10400 / National Building Regulations issued by the municipal fire authority (e.g., Johannesburg Emergency Management Services), including annual inspection and evacuation plan; structural load assessment for server rooms and electronic equipment racks; and compliance with the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993, evidenced by a Certificate of Compliance or Letter of Good Standing from the Department of Employment and Labour prior to occupation of the registered office premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) – eFiling portal (www.sars.gov.za)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must register with SARS by submitting the foreign company incorporation certificate, completed IT150 (company income tax registration) and VAT101 (if VAT registration sought), together with a power of attorney for a SARS-accredited representative or local public officer. Registration is effected via eFiling or at a SARS branch, producing an income tax reference number and, where applicable, a VAT reference number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not operate a check-the-box entity classification regime. Companies are taxable per se as residents or non-resident entities. Specific statutory elections exist for intra-group transactions, controlled foreign company inclusions, and hybrid mismatch adjustments, all governed by the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962 and the Taxation Laws Amendment Acts.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration: cumulative taxable supplies exceeding ZAR 1,000,000 in the preceding 12 months. Voluntary registration: cumulative supplies of ZAR 50,000 in the preceding 12 months.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping mandate. Tax invoices must satisfy section 20 of the VAT Act 89 of 1991 and be issued electronically or on paper. SARS mandates electronic filing and digital record submission through eFiling, with progressive data-driven compliance monitoring.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of movable goods qualify for zero-rating under section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act if the supplier has exported the goods within the prescribed period and holds evidence of export. Export of services qualifies under section 11(2)(l) where the services are supplied to a non-resident and the services are physically performed outside South Africa or are directly related to exported goods, provided the non-resident is not a South African resident and the services are not consumed in South Africa.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Airway Bill
Proof of Export (terminal receipt / port clearance)
Bank Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign currency deposit evidence
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent export zero-rating claims attract retrospective VAT clawback with interest under section 14 of the VAT Act, an additional 200% penalty under section 233 of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 for substantial understatements, and criminal prosecution under section 234 of the Tax Administration Act with fines up to ZAR 5 million or imprisonment up to 5 years. SARS applies heightened documentary verification for crowdfunding-platform service exports.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), specifically the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), acting under the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933 and the Exchange Control Regulations 1961, with operational delegation to Authorised Dealers (registered commercial banks) and Authorised Dealers in Foreign Exchange with Limited Authority (ADLAs).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: ZAR is fully convertible for current account transactions, including brokerage fees, technology subscription fees, and administrative expenses, subject only to an Authorised Dealer declaration with supporting invoices. Capital account inflows for inward foreign direct investment (equity subscription into the Pty Ltd) by non-residents are freely permitted without prior FinSurv approval, but must be registered with an Authorised Dealer to obtain a Foreign Investment (FI) declaration enabling future dividend and disinvestment remittance. Outbound capital account transfers (foreign venture investments, intercompany loans, loan repayments, offshore treasury placements) require Sub-Limit approval per Authorised Dealer or FinSurv approval where the corporate limit is exceeded. Profit and dividend remittance hurdles are materially manageable: a non-resident shareholder may remit dividends upon presentation of the FI declaration, audited or reviewed financial statements confirming distributable reserves, a valid SARS tax clearance certificate for foreign payments (CSD/PIN), and evidence of no adverse sanctions or FATF-linked screening. The platform must also demonstrate that each crowdfunding investor holds beneficial ownership that is not obscured by nominee structures, and that the investment complied with the FSCA equity crowdfunding per-investor limits, if applicable.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Statutory timeline: all export proceeds, including service fees and platform commissions earned from non-residents in the SACU corridor, must be received in South Africa within 180 days from the date of shipment or service completion, unless extended by the Authorised Dealer or FinSurv. Mandatory conversion ratio: none, the historical 100% surrender requirement was abolished in 2010, therefore the conversion ratio is 0%; however, the repatriation obligation is 100% of the invoiced export value, and the proceeds may be credited to a Foreign Currency Account (FCA) held with an Authorised Dealer. Reduced or non-receipt of proceeds must be reported with a non-receipt certificate in terms of the Currency and Exchanges Manual.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for primary settlement custody and Low-Medium as ancillary payout rails. Offshore digital EMIs and cross-border payment platforms (e.g., Wise Business, Payoneer, Currencycloud) are not authorised to take deposits or hold client monies in South Africa under the Banks Act 94 of 1990 and cannot host the ring-fenced crowdfunding escrow. They may be engaged only as technical payment gateways intermediated by a licensed Authorised Dealer, and must comply with FICA due diligence data requirements. South African PSPs registered under the National Payment System Act 78 of 1998 may process collections/disbursements, but the final settlement of funds in ECF transactions must be in a bank account with a registered bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is mandatory for all directors, all shareholders holding 5% or more, and all ultimate beneficial owners at the Authorised Dealer corporate branch for the initial onboarding of a High_Risk_Special_License entity. In-person identity verification, biometric fingerprint capture, original board resolution, and notarised/certified copies of constitutional documents are required. Remote opening is generally not permitted for the first relationship; however, after the first onboarding, further signatory changes may be effected via secure electronic mandates with video verification. The completion of a live FSCA licence verification through the FSCA registry is a non-waivable bank precondition.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Public collection of funds from an open retail investor base without clear exemption from deposit-taking provisions, triggering Banks Act and collective investment scheme red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) FSCA Category I FSP licence under the FAIS Act 37 of 2002 with ECF scope; (ii) legal opinion confirming qualification as a securities intermediary under the FAIS Act and the Companies Act 71 of 2008; (iii) FICA registration certificate as an accountable institution with the Financial Intelligence Centre; (iv) funding structure of ECF campaigns showing that funds are held in trust and released only upon target threshold; (v) SARB/G20 confirmation of no required banking licence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party money concentration: multiple unknown investors remitting into a single account with insufficient beneficial ownership transparency, a money-laundering structuring red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Ring-fenced trust account mandate executed under section 20 of the FAIS Act or section 4(1)(b) of the Banks Act; (ii) daily reconciliation reports per crowdfunding campaign; (iii) whitelist of verified ECF investors with IDs and PEP/sanctions screening logs; (iv) source-of-funds declarations and proof of bank account verification for each investor; (v) documented FICA risk management and compliance monitoring programme.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound foreign capital attributed to high-risk jurisdictions, shell-company investors, or politically exposed persons with no economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Beneficial ownership register filed with CIPC; (ii) declared FI registration with the Authorised Dealer (Form A.200); (iii) entity substance evidence for corporate investors: audited financials, local physical address, business registry extract; (iv) adverse media and sanctions screening results; (v) shareholder declarations of tax residence and source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Association with crypto-assets, tokenised securities, or cash-intensive settlement rails, which many SA banks auto-decline for ECF platforms.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Written confirmation that no crypto or token settlement is offered; (ii) specification of bank-wire and ACH/Escrow-only rails in the operating manual; (iii) prohibition of cash or bearer instruments in the platform terms; (iv) system audit trail showing all pay-in/pay-out events via named bank accounts; (v) an independent forensic readiness report prepared by an AML consultant.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident investors subscribe by SWIFT MT103 wire to the Pty Ltd ZAR account (or USD conversion account) at the Authorised Dealer. The compliant protocol is: (i) receive full KYC/beneficial ownership pack on the non-resident investor; (ii) wire reference carries purpose code 5211 Direct Investment - Equity Capital in the ZAR BOP reporting, with narrative 'Share subscription - ordinary shares'; (iii) the Authorised Dealer registers the inward FDI in the SARB Extranet and issues the Foreign Investment (FI) declaration to the company, a precondition for future dividend and disinvestment remittances; (iv) for crowdfunding investors below the FSCA per-investor cap, simplified EDD applies, but each investor must be individually identifiable and reconciled in the escrow ledger; (v) CIPC share allotment under sections 39 and 40 of the Companies Act is completed within statutory timelines; (vi) escrow funds are released to the issuer only after the offer threshold is met, with failed-campaign funds returned via reversing MT103 to the originating investor account. Any investment routed through offshore holding jurisdictions requires an additional economic substance questionnaire to the Authorised Dealer.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operating and technology service payments to non-residents are cleared via SWIFT MT103 through the Authorised Dealer, supported by proforma invoice, service contract, and SARS tax clearance. Commercial trade settlements in the SACU corridor use Letter of Credit (MT700 issuance, confirmation, or negotiation) with Standard Bank or Nedbank trade desks. ECF platform payouts to domestic investee companies are effected through the local ACH/EAC (Electronic Account Confirmation) or ISO 20022 (SAMOS) rails, while any return of capital to non-resident investors uses MT103 with Form A.300 and the FI declaration. For high-value disbursements, banks apply dual-approval mandates and reference the treasury script to avoid exchange control mismatches.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore forward exchange contracts (FECs) with the Authorised Dealer for committed trade and fee exposures, typically up to 12 months tenor, under the Currency and Exchanges Manual for Authorised Dealers.
Offshore ZAR non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) transacted by non-resident counterparties as hedging overlay; onshore NDFs are not available to residents without FinSurv approval.
Cross-currency swaps (USD/ZAR and EUR/ZAR) between the corporate and an Authorised Dealer to hedge loan principal or long-term equity bridge exposure, subject to underlying transaction evidence.
Currency options purchased from the Authorised Dealer for protection on anticipated ECF fee receipts; sale or structuring of options by residents requires FinSurv consent.
FX swaps for short-term liquidity management of the escrow and operational pools, restricted to genuine commercial flow and subject to daily SARB balance report.
Foreign Currency Account (FCA) balances with the Authorised Dealer to retain export proceeds and platform revenues in USD/EUR without mandatory conversion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after each anniversary of the company's incorporation date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of ZAR 500 per month; continued non-compliance triggers a CIPC compliance notice, final demand, and administrative strike-off under section 82 of the Companies Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (renewal of beneficial ownership record)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted concurrently with the annual return, within 30 business days after each incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm beneficial ownership constitutes a compliance breach under the Companies Act and the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act, subject to administrative fines and possible criminal liability for officers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Compliance Report (FAIS Act - FSP compliance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 calendar days after the company's financial year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalty up to ZAR 5 million per contravention; suspension or conditional renewal of the financial services provider license; possible debarment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit required if the company's public interest score is at least 350; for scores between 100 and 349, a financial review is required; a private company with no public interest score above 99 may opt for an independent review unless the MOI or shareholders require a formal audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (IFRS as adopted by the International Accounting Standards Board) or IFRS for SMEs depending on the company's public interest score and regulatory license conditions; the FSCA generally requires financial statements prepared on IFRS standards for licensed FSPs.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must annually confirm the identity, percentage of ownership and control, and nature of control of every beneficial owner; any changes during the year must be filed with CIPC within 5 business days; incomplete or false annual confirmation renders the company liable to fines and director disqualification.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and prescribed officers
Register of Remuneration and Committees (where applicable)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 180 - USD 450 per year for a standard registered office and registered agent service in South Africa
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - USD 12,000 depending on turnover, transactional volume and internal control complexity of the equity crowdfunding portal

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No industry-specific tax holiday for crowdfunding intermediaries. General incentives available: Section 11D R&D allowance (150% of qualifying expenditure), 80% annual set-off cap for assessed losses, and employment-related incentives (e.g., Employment Tax Incentive) if applicable. No reduced preferential corporate rate is applicable to Standard (Pty) Ltd.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (no statutory expiry; applied against taxable income subject to 80% annual offset cap)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 – Income Tax Return for Companies via SARS eFiling
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The ITR14 must be submitted within 12 months of the financial year-end. Provisional tax payments are generally due at the end of the sixth month of the year of assessment, at the end of the tax year, and six months after the tax year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity name, South African income tax reference number, financial year start/end dates, company registration number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the SARS tax branch reference for the South African branch or permanent establishment; mark non-resident status only if the company is foreign incorporated. A local branch must specify the PE's registered tax number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Domestic trading income, platform commission, listing fees, escrow-related service fees, and other business receipts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only income having a South African source. For a non-resident operator, income derived from South African users or a SA PE must be disclosed with full operational detail.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income from offshore investors or non-South African issuers, foreign dividends, interest, royalties, and other worldwide income of a resident company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with a SA PE must declare foreign income only to the extent attributable to that PE and exempt under the applicable DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt dividends, interest from local/foreign sources qualifying for exemption, and other statutory exemptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exemptions are rarely available to non-residents. Ensure compliance with DTA source and beneficial ownership conditions before claiming exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses, salaries, marketing, software, compliance, FSCA licensing fees, escrow and AML compliance costs, and Section 11D R&D claims.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE may deduct expenses directly attributable to the PE. Head-office charges require compliance with the transfer pricing and arm’s-length documentation rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after exemptions and deductions, with assessed loss carried forward applied subject to the 80% cap.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident PE is taxed on its SA-source attributable profits; assessed losses are limited to the PE's trading operations and may not be combined with offshore losses without TP review.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporation tax at 27% on taxable income, net of provisional tax payments, PAYE withholding, and withholding tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents are assessed at the same 27% rate on PE-attributable income. Any tax withheld by payer clients (e.g., royalties) is claimable as a credit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an administrative penalty under s210/s211 of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011: a fixed R250-per-month penalty (per return) for small/medium taxpayers, and for larger taxpayers a percentage-based 'understatement penalty' of 10%-200% of the tax shortfall (depending on conduct) or a dynamic monthly penalty. Deliberate non-filing may trigger criminal prosecution with fines up to ZAR 10 million and imprisonment up to 10 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced treaty rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must: (1) complete and sign the SARS Declaration on Dividends Tax (DTD) confirming beneficial ownership; (2) submit a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority; (3) deliver both to the South African distributing company before the dividend payment is made. The company then withholds at the treaty rate, subject to a SARS directive in exceptional cases. Documentation must be retained by the paying company for 5 years; failure to obtain declaration may result in under-deduction and entity liability for the shortfall plus penalties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory withholding tax of 15%; treaty rates typically 0% (arm's-length finance) or 10% under targeted DTAs. Royalties: statutory WHT of 15%; treaty rates generally 0% (copyright) or 10% (industrial/ commercial royalties). Domestic law may exempt qualifying interest paid to a lender approved under the DTA.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: required for any cross-border controlled (related-party) transactions with an annual aggregate value equal to or exceeding ZAR 100 million; Master File / CbC Report: mandatory where the multinational group's consolidated revenue is equal to or exceeds ZAR 10 billion. Lower thresholds apply to designated 'high risk' transactions, e.g., interest-bearing loans where ZAR 5 million triggers a transfer pricing disclosure.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Valuation techniques for intangibles and financial transactions
Comparable profits method in exceptional circumstances
Advance Pricing Agreement (APA) as a compliance tool
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa does not have a standalone Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) akin to some offshore jurisdictions. However, Section 31 of the Income Tax Act mandates that transfer pricing adjustments apply to actual economic substance rather than the legal form. SARS will disregard a scheme if the substance demonstrates a paper/conduit arrangement without commercial rationale. In addition, the general anti-avoidance rule in Section 103(1) of the ITA applies to nullify any tax avoidance scheme lacking substance, and the 'GAAR' rules in Sections 80A-80L similarly collapse abusive transactions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Systematically understating crowdfunding commission income, omitting escrow interest revenue, creating fictitious deduction invoices, or failing to register for income tax while operating the portal.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Tax Administration Act 28/2011, a 'false or misleading return' can result in a criminally imposed fine up to ZAR 10 million and/or imprisonment up to 5 years. SARS also imposes an understatement penalty ranging from 10% to 200% of the assessed shortfall plus interest (currently 10.5%). Where a director knowingly participated, joint liability attaches directly to the responsible officer.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a solvent company can be held personally liable for unpaid SARS debt under 'representative taxpayer' provisions, travel bans may be sought via a Section 162 order for debts exceeding ZAR 50,000; civil restitution, removal from the board, and criminal prosecution can follow.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an equity crowdfunding portal without a FSCA Financial Services Provider (FSP) license or without an approved 'responsible person' and working capital as required under the Financial Advisory and Intermediary Services Act (FAIS Act) and Crowdfunding guidance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Financial Markets Act 19 of 2012 and FAIS Act, unlicensed activity may attract an administrative penaly up to ZAR 15 million; criminal conviction can result in imprisonment up to 10 years; the FSCA may order compensation to investors and seizure of commissions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for unpaid penalties if they knowingly caused the portal to accept regulated investments. They may be banned from acting as directors for up to 10 years and face civil claims by investors for proceeds received, plus disgorgement of profits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Arrangement / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a (Pty) Ltd that has no employees, no physical office, no board meetings in South Africa, and merely functions as a conduit for foreign escrow or intercompany financing from connected intermediaries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS will disregard the shell for tax purposes under Section 80A-80L (GAAR) and recompute taxable income at fair arm's-length levels; this triggers additional 27% tax, interest at 10.5%, and understatement penalties of 100%-200%. A shell also faces CIPC deregistration under the Companies Act 71 of 2008 and loss of corporate veil when used to commit fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under the Companies Act 71/2008 s77(3), directors may be personally liable for reckless or fraudulent conduct, including use of a shell to misrepresent investor rights. Directors can be interdicted from leaving the Republic, and criminal negligence can lead to imprisonment up to 4 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to perform client due diligence on startup issuers and investors, allowing escrow ACH/Wire facilities to be used for round-tripping or excessive cash flows, or not reporting suspicious transactions to the Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2011 imposes administrative sanctions up to ZAR 10 million per contravention. The FIC can also issue a directive, remove the accountable institution from the list, and refer to the NPA for money laundering prosecution under the Prevention of Organised Crime Act (POCA) – offence carries imprisonment up to 15 years for directors acting in good faith without reasonable grounds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for AML penalties if the corporation fails to implement an AML programme (risk management, training, KYC, record keeping). Courts may pierce the corporate veil, enforcing civil recovery orders and attaching personal assets where the portal was used as a vehicle for money laundering or terror finance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Invoicing management fees, technology licensing, or platform fees from a related shell entity to a low-tax jurisdiction, or artificially structured loans to South African crowdfunding entities without economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS will adjust 'affected transactions' under Section 31 on an arm's-length basis; interest and penalties of up to 200% apply. Treaties may be denied where the transaction lacks bonafide substance; the DTA beneficial ownership test may also be rejected, resulting in 20% dividends WHT (rather than 5%) and 15% WHT on royalties/interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who prepared/signed false TP documentation face criminal liability under s235 TAA; civil restitution to the Crown for underpaid tax can be recovered from directors who knowingly participated in the scheme, and travel restrictions may apply during SARS investigations.
